has undertaken to coordinate the naming of a bridge in each town after our veterans. I think this is a wonderful way to remember our veterans and I hope the committee does as well.

The next three bills are codifying the colloquial name for each of the bridges. You will notice I
brought forth an amendment. My office was originally under the impression that these bills already had names but were waiting for signs. Maine DOT notified me that these bridges never
had official names. The amendment includes the official naming of each of these bridges.

LD 2184 officially names the Warren's Bridge in Cornish and South Hiram. The Warren's Bridge
is named after Col. Joseph Warren, He owned a grist mill off a pond near this bridge. Both Hiram and Cornish noted that when this bridge was first built in 1929, it had a sign displaying the name
"Warren's Bridge." The bridge serves as an important link between the two communities, and -
officially naming it will help memorialize the history of this area.`

need for better signage to denote the bridge. The Town of Standish said that the lack of signage
can "lead to confusion for individual unfamiliar with the area, particularly in situations requiring

Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts and distinguished members of the Joint Standing
Committee on Transportation, I am Meghan Russo, Director of Govermnent Affairs at
MaineDOT. MaineDOT is neither for nor against LD 2184, LD 2185, and LD 2186, but would
like to recommend the committee consider amending these bills.
MaineDOT considers the naming of bridges, roadways, and other state transportation
infrastructure to be within the purview of the Legislature. Once a legislative bill has passed
officially naming a piece of transportation infrastructure MaineDOT will erect the appropriate signage. Our records indicate these three bridges have not been officially named by the legislature. In order to erect the requested signs, we request the committee amend these bills to legislatively name the structures. Once that occurs, we would be happy to erect the signage.
Thank you.
